# Kind support per target and channel

> **Back to:** [README](../../README.md) · [Documentation index](../index.md)

Which artifact kinds each target delivers on each channel. `scaffold` = files written into a
project by `sigil add` (and the target's `sigil build` layout); `plugin` = marketplace plugins
built by `sigil build`. `native` = emitted as its own file or config fragment; `via inline` =
carried inside the skills that `uses:` it; `—` = not delivered (see the numbered note). Why the
channels are split this way: [distribution-channels-2026-09](../decisions/distribution-channels-2026-09.md).

## scaffold

| Kind | claude | copilot | agents-standard | codex | cursor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mcp | native | native | — (1) | native | — (2) |
| hook | native | native | — (3) | native | native |
| settings | native | — (4) | — (5) | — (6) | — (6) |
| prompt | native | native | — (7) | — (8) | — (9) |
| skill | native | native | native | native | native |
| agent | native | native | — (10) | — (11) | — (12) |
| rule | native | native | via inline (13) | via inline (14) | native |
| workflow | native | native | — (15) | — (16) | — (17) |
| template | — (18) | — (18) | — (18) | — (18) | — (18) |

1. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no MCP config file shared by its tools; install it for a tool-specific target
2. not built yet — [Cursor — Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp)
3. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no hooks; install it for a tool-specific target
4. this kind's schema is Claude Code's own vocabulary — sigil has no Copilot emitter for it
5. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no settings; install it for a tool-specific target
6. this kind's schema is Claude Code's own vocabulary
7. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no user-invoked prompts with arguments; install it for a tool-specific target
8. Codex custom prompts are deprecated in favor of skills — [OpenAI Codex — Custom prompts](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/custom-prompts)
9. Cursor is folding commands into skills (/migrate-to-skills) — [Cursor — Commands](https://cursor.com/docs/context/commands)
10. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no subagents; install it for a tool-specific target
11. a Codex agent file can't restrict tools, so a catalog agent would gain every tool — [OpenAI Codex — Subagents](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents)
12. not built yet: a Cursor subagent has no tool list, so a read-only one needs `readonly: true` — [Cursor — Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/context/subagents)
13. folded into each skill that `uses:` it — [Agent Skills — the open standard](https://agentskills.io)
14. folded into each skill that `uses:` it — [OpenAI Codex — Build skills](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills)
15. the open standard (Agent Skills, AGENTS.md) defines no workflows; install it for a tool-specific target
16. Codex has no workflow file
17. Cursor has no workflow file
18. templates are composed into other artifacts at resolve time, never emitted
